headline: Dealing with Unfinished Walls: What to Know Before You Paint
articleBody:
So, you've got unfinished walls, maybe after a demolition or a new addition in your Berkeley or East Bay home, and you're ready to add some color. While it might seem like you can just slap on some paint, proper preparation is actually the secret sauce to a beautiful, long-lasting finish. Skipping steps now will only lead to headaches later!

First, a thorough inspection is crucial. Look for any signs of moisture, peeling, cracks, or holes. These aren't just cosmetic issues; they can prevent paint from adhering properly. You'll need to repair any damaged substrates and ensure the surfaces are clean, dry, and free of dust or grease. This often involves cleaning, patching, sanding, and sometimes even specialized repairs for moisture damage. Once everything is smooth and clean, protecting your floors, fixtures, and adjacent areas is a must. Masking tape and drop cloths are your best friends here. Don't forget to remove or carefully mask any hardware like light switches or outlet covers.

What to Expect During the Process:
After prep, areas that have been repaired or are incompatible with your topcoat will need priming. This ensures better adhesion, a more uniform color, and can seal in any stains or odors. Applying the specified number of coats under suitable temperature and humidity conditions is next. Rushing the recoat time between layers is a common mistake that can lead to a less durable finish. Once the paint is dry, careful removal of masking and a thorough inspection under consistent lighting will reveal any areas needing touch-ups. Remember, even if the paint is 'dry to touch,' it might not be fully cured, so follow product guidelines for occupancy.
